business_summary.text: Karamtara Engineering manufactures lattice transmission towers, solar mounting structures and trackers, wind towers and fasteners, with 13 manufacturing facilities across India and Italy and exports to over 50 countries.

call_points.text: FY27 revenue growth guided at 60-65% over FY26.
No FY28 revenue guidance; management said it will speak more as the year pans out.
Q1 EBITDA margin was 11%, hit by high freight and local delivery costs; margins expected to improve as assets are sweated.
Q1FY26 EBITDA margin was 13%; management declined to give a specific margin target.
Bhuj facility started; peak capacity expected in next 6-9 months.
PEB facility for data centres expected to start by beginning of next financial year.
FY26 EBITDA was about ₹500 Cr and cash conversion about ₹675 Cr.
Q1 sales volume was about 135,000 tons.

operating_notes.text: Installed capacity stood at 889,200 metric tons per annum as of Q1FY27, excluding captive rolling and galvanizing.
Q1FY27 sales volume was about 135,000 tons.
US tariff cost in Q1FY27 was about ₹250 Cr, part of other expenses, fully passed through to customers.
FY26 sales volume was 3.90 million MTPA (FY25: 2.92 million MTPA), with EBITDA/tonne of INR12,844 (INR11,890).
Net working capital cycle was 143 days in FY26 (FY25: 165 days), with free cash flow negative INR4,379 million in FY26.
Saudi Arabia project cost is estimated at INR4,050 million, with INR3,300 million debt sanctioned and about INR2,000 million disbursed; it is set to add 0.22 million MTPA and start revenue from FY28.

timeline.summary: Karamtara Engineering held its first post-listing earnings call on October 7, 2026, reporting Q1FY27 revenue of ₹1,581 Cr (up 72% YoY) and guiding FY27 revenue growth of 60-65%.
Board approved incorporation of wholly owned subsidiary Karamtara Defence & Aerospace Limited for defence and aerospace manufacturing.

India Ratings upgraded Karamtara Engineering's long-term bank loan rating to IND AA-/Stable from IND A+ and short-term rating to IND A1+ from IND A1 on ₹2,432 Cr of facilities, citing larger scale, IPO-led debt repayment and a ₹6,000 Cr order book.
Karamtara Engineering secured new orders aggregating approximately ₹1,199 Cr across transmission and renewable energy segments on October 27, 2026.
